http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26157v1.abstract: Long-horizon agentic tasks require a model to call tools over many steps at contexts of 100K tokens or more, yet many low-bit quantization methods are calibrated on short web text and judged on perplexity. This mismatch is costly: existing quantizations of Qwen3.8-27B at or below 3 bits per weight match BF16 on shorter tasks like AIME, yet in published results solve at most 72% as many tasks as BF16 on DeepSWE, a long-horizon agentic benchmark. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26553v1.title: Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation (ROGUE-AI)
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26553v1.abstract: Agents based on large language models (LLMs) can now delete files and send payments on behalf of their users. News media reports routinely describe failures of these agents (e.g., Replit's coding agent deleting a production database), but a report often only says what went wrong and rarely (in)validates the incident or finds its root cause. Incident catalogs collect these reports, and benchmarks record whether agents fail, but neither replicates an incident nor tests the cause its report might identify. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26361v1.title: How Much Should an Agent Remember? Deployment Lessons from Self-Distilled Memory for LLM Agents
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26361v1.abstract: LLM agents on long-horizon tasks fail in recurring, procedural ways. They mis-paginate an API, resolve the wrong entity, or answer when no answer was asked. We built a pipeline that lets an agent learn from its own history. It first mines short \emph{lessons} from the agent's own trajectories, one to three per episode. It then consolidates those lessons into a smaller set of \emph{guidelines}, where each guideline records how many lessons it merged. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25380v1.title: Beyond Weight Updates: Evolving Agent Harnesses for Domain Specialization
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25380v1.abstract: Domain specialization of LLM agents is usually framed as a weight-update problem: collect trajectories, run reinforcement learning (RL) or supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and deploy a new checkpoint. We study a complementary axis: evolving the \textbf{agent harness}---the system prompt, tool schemas, skill library, and planning scaffolding---while keeping the policy frozen. We cast harness evolution as an RL-style outer loop and instantiate it with GEPA, a reflective evolutionary optimizer. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25360v1.title: AppSci-Bench: Can LLMs Build AI Agents and Make Them Better?
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25360v1.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used not only to power AI agents but also to build them. While many benchmarks assess the quality of LLM- powered agents, few ascertain how good LLMs are at building them. To this end, we introduce AppSci-Bench, where we construct a setting akin to how human Applied Scientists build agents for businesses - through eliciting task requirements from stakeholders, exploring the business's infrastructure, and scientifically improve the target agent by designing experiments and internal benchmarks. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25526v1.title: MATE: Mobile Agent Trustworthy Execution for Safe and Efficient Mobile Control
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25526v1.abstract: Mobile agents on personal smartphones can affect private data, payments, settings, and the foreground screen. We present MATE (Mobile Agent Trustworthy Execution), an execution-layer system that controls the boundary between agent action proposals and device effects without modifying the underlying model. MATE represents each UI primitive as a structured action record that combines the instruction, target app, screen context, primitive, and action fields. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25534v1.abstract: Agent skills are documents in which experts write down procedural knowledge, and models increasingly maintain them by rewriting them without feedback. Such rewriting could adapt a skill to the model that uses it or erode the expert knowledge that makes it useful, yet how skills evolve under this feedback-free self-evolution has not been studied. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26423v1.title: Seer: Guiding Small Deep-Research Agents with Shared Decision Models
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26423v1.abstract: Deep-research agents repeatedly decide what to search, read, and verify, often using large cloud-hosted language models for action proposal. However, privacy and local control motivate running agents on users' devices, where limited memory and compute favor smaller models and complicate on-device training. Yet inference-time guidance faces three obstacles: exploring alternatives through real execution adds tool calls, prompted self-evaluation is bounded by the agent's judgment, and model-specific guidance risks repeated adaptation costs. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25429v1.title: Evolve Where It Matters: Coverage-Guided Self-Evolution of Agent Skills
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25429v1.abstract: Agent skills package procedural knowledge as natural-language instructions, and a skill helps only when its instructions are correct and properly followed by the agent. Self-evolving agents revise their own skills from the runs they make, but existing methods judge each run as a whole, by its outcome or by where it went wrong, and cannot tell whether a failure comes from a wrong instruction or from one the agent did not follow. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25412v1.title: ChainAgent: Automated Chainable Vulnerability Discovery in PHP Web Applications
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25412v1.abstract: High-impact attacks on PHP web applications often chain limited-capability vulnerabilities with other flaws or intended behaviors. Discovering these chains requires identifying flaws and the dependencies enabling capability composition. Existing vulnerability discovery techniques analyze flaws in isolation, while attack planning assumes known components. This separation makes it difficult to discover previously unknown components whose security relevance becomes apparent only through their potential roles in an exploit chain. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26069v1.title: SheetAlign: Grounded Interaction and Stage-Isolated Learning for Spreadsheet Agents
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26069v1.abstract: Spreadsheets are widely used for data analysis and supporting decision-making. Automating spreadsheet analysis while protecting sensitive data and controlling deployment costs motivates locally deployed open-weight large language models (LLMs). Meanwhile, complex spreadsheet tasks require both task reasoning and workbook understanding, while predefined operation interfaces impose additional tool-selection and invocation demands. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25088v1.title: BuggyMLE: Scaling Machine Learning Engineering Difficulty with Bug Injection
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25088v1.abstract: Enabling AI systems to autonomously improve AI models requires agents capable of performing machine learning engineering (MLE). In practice, designing, training, and evaluating complex models demands modifying multi-file repositories to reproduce results, debug training runs, integrate datasets, and port frameworks. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25680v1.title: Beyond Entity Recognition: Vision-Centric Knowledge Visual Question Answering
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25680v1.abstract: We propose VC-VQA, a large-scale benchmark for vision-centric knowledge reasoning, aiming to systematically evaluate the capabilities of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in fine-grained visual knowledge acquisition and complex multi-stage reasoning. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25123v1.title: Forget Freely, Grep Later: Lossless, Index-Free Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25123v1.abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents often exceed their context windows, forcing them to discard information that may be needed later. Existing context management strategies rely on summarization, masking, or structured memory, requiring decisions about what to preserve or how to retrieve it before future needs are known. However, these methods can introduce lossy compression, potentially discarding details needed for future tasks. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25257v1.abstract: Can a frontier model repair a vision-language model (VLM) by rewriting its weights? Small reasoning VLMs such as Qwen3.5 need such a repair: in thinking mode they fall into loops on many image questions, repeating themselves until the token limit, spending the whole budget and losing the answer. The usual remedies act on the decoding, leaving the looping model as it was, or must be told what to change. Yet the cause is written in the weights. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27294v1.title: HookEvo: A Framework for Coordinated Plugin Evolution on Hook-Enabled Agent Runtimes
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27294v1.abstract: Repairing failures in tool-using agents can require coordinated changes to how the harness interprets tool receipts, assembles context, and checks actions. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27139v1.title: Do Senior Agents Do Their Job? Measuring Role Integrity in How LLM Agents Use Subordinate Material
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27139v1.abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems increasingly divide long tasks among subagents whose reports a senior agent turns into the final answer. Such a division of labor pays off only if each agent, and above all the senior agent, carries out the duties of its role. Current evaluations, however, mostly score the final answer, and a fluent, well-cited answer cannot show whether the senior agent weighed its subagents' reports or merely aggregated them. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27046v1.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Stateful Privacy Sniffing of LLM Agents via Behavioral Covert Channels in Web Interactions
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27046v1.abstract: LLM agents increasingly rely on Web interaction, issuing searches, following links, and reading pages, to complete complex user tasks. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27483v1.title: From Manufacturing Event Logs to Simulation: Enabling SMEs with Agentic AI for SimPy Simulation Generation
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27483v1.abstract: High expertise and cost barriers exclude small and medium-sized enterprises from discrete-event simulation (DES). http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26980v1.abstract: LLM agents such as Hermes, OpenClaw, and Codex repeatedly resend growing execution histories, increasing shared GPU key-value (KV) cache demand in high-bandwidth memory (HBM). http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26722v1.abstract: To autonomously execute multi-step tasks, enterprise agents must reliably interact with tools, call APIs, or query databases, making tool-calling a fundamental capability of AI models. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27734v1.title: AutoOntologyBench: A Task-Grounded Benchmark for Agentic Knowledge Engineering
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27734v1.abstract: Foundation-model agents are increasingly extending beyond software engineering (SWE) into autonomous scientific research, where acquiring and integrating domain knowledge remains a critical challenge. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27196v1.abstract: GPU acceleration has transformed electronic design automation (EDA), yet further improving expert-engineered GPU tools still demands substantial manual effort. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27839v1.abstract: Multi-agent systems for scientific claim verification increasingly rely on role-structured LLM debate to pressure-test hypotheses. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27876v1.title: LesionAgent: Training-Free Agentic Tumor Tracking and Response Assessment in Longitudinal CT
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27876v1.abstract: Every few months, a cancer patient's CT scans decide whether treatment continues. 3D foundation models can now detect, segment, register and track lesions, yet none of them reads the scans as a radiologist does. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27095v1.abstract: Language-model agents using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) face three runtime verification gaps: (i) action fabrication, where post-tool prose narrates side effects that failed, timed out, or never ran; (ii) provenance collapse, where unverified model prose or web text enters durable memory alongside executed tool outputs; and (iii) syndicated echo amplification, where mirrored web pages satisfy multi-source corroboration from one origin. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26897v1.abstract: Improving agents requires discovering where they fail and understanding why. An agent acts over multiple steps in a changing environment, so diagnosing its failures requires more than inspecting the final response of a large language model (LLM). http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26910v1.title: AstronautBench: Measuring Agent Self-Improvement Across Episodes Through Knowledge, Evidence, and Progress
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26910v1.abstract: LLM agents are expected to improve themselves from their own experience across episodes, with fixed weights. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27222v1.title: Bel: Step-Level Policy Improvement of Visual Agents Without Training
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27222v1.abstract: A visual agent acts on what it sees: it taps and types on a screen, or points on a camera image to show a robot where to act. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28341v1.title: When Tools Fail, Agents Fabricate: Silent Failure and Verification-First Oversight in Tool-Using LLM Agents
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28341v1.abstract: Tool-using LLM agents must recover when a tool call fails, by retrying, switching tools, or revising their plan. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28574v1.title: EvoViM: Recursively Self-Evolving Visual Agents for Exploration with Deferred Queries
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28574v1.abstract: Multimodal large language model (MLLM) agents have shown promising capabilities in task-oriented environments. However, they still struggle when queries are deferred until after exploration, requiring them to retain visual evidence before knowing which details will matter. We introduce EvoViM, a recursively self-evolving framework in which a frozen multimodal model turns its own interaction experience into one visual program for memory and skills. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28957v1.abstract: It is now common practice in software development for large language models (LLMs) to be used to generate program code. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28542v1.title: BIRD-Persona: A Persona-Aware Benchmark for SQL and pandas Analytics Code Generation
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28542v1.abstract: Production text-to-code systems use large language models to turn natural-language analytics requests into executable SQL and pandas code. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31185v1.title: CO-GRAFT: Attributing Reinforcement Learning Gains in Search Agents via Role-Level Policy Grafting
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31185v1.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) improves large language model search agents by up to 32 exact-match (EM) points over their pre-RL initializations, yet overall accuracy gains do not identify which underlying functional capabilities improve or interact during training. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31198v1.abstract: Recent multimodal search agents use reasoning, vision, and live web search across many turns to answer questions beyond parametric knowledge by orchestrating a small library of hand-crafted search and visual tools. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29009v1.title: Mind the Trap As LLMs Guess the Data Model: Grain-Aware Guards Against Fan-out in Text-to-SQL and Its Benchmarks

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28420v1.abstract: The advancement of large language models (LLMs) has significantly enhanced the capabilities of agents across various tasks. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29062v1.abstract: Personalized LLM agents rely on an agent harness, the surrounding memory and control code, to connect user history with downstream decisions. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30624v1.title: Oops!... I Parsed It Again: Tool-Call Smuggling Against LLM Agents
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30624v1.abstract: LLM agents act through tool calls: the model writes the arguments of a call as JSON, a guard decides whether the call may run, and an executor runs it. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29367v1.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) need evaluations of everyday reasoning and tool use, such as planning itineraries under user constraints and grounding numerical answers in evidence. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31063v1.title: From Local Errors to System Failures: Modeling and Benchmarking Error Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.32917v1.abstract: Deep search agents address complex information needs through iterative retrieval and reasoning, where the relevance of retrieved evidence influences downstream performance. Existing rerankers improve retrieval effectiveness but introduce substantial latency and cost when invoked throughout the search trajectory. We introduce SOARS, a training-free framework leveraging a System One model for fast, calibrated relevance estimation. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31668v1.title: Provenance Loss and Repair in Multilingual Compaction

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31586v1.title: SecondChance: Benchmarking Reliable Error Recovery in AI Agents
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31586v1.abstract: AI agents make errors while they act, and their reliability depends on what they do afterwards. Existing recovery benchmarks mostly inject faults, involve no user and score whether the task is eventually completed, so they cannot show whether an agent undid its own silent error, told the user, or faced an error that could not be fixed. We introduce SecondChance, an error checkpoint dataset and evaluation harness that profiles and measures error-recovery behaviour of AI agents. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31727v1.title: fork() for Agents: Agent Kernel for Non-blocking LLM Orchestration
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31727v1.abstract: LLM-based agents typically execute tool calls synchronously and discard completed work upon failure. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.32246v1.abstract: Runtime skills can improve agents' problem-solving capabilities by providing procedural guidance for tasks such as code review and debugging. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.32946v1.abstract: The use of AI agents among the general public has been increasing exponentially throughout 2026, though it is often hard for users to determine which configuration is most effective for their personal use. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31582v1.abstract: Latent interfaces let agents in a multi-agent system communicate through continuous representations rather than decoded text. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.33148v1.abstract: Reasoning models become long-horizon agents through reinforcement learning or, more cheaply, through fine-tuning on a stronger teacher's trajectories, which contain the teacher's chain-of-thought as well as its actions. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31427v1.title: Learning What vs. Learning How: Decomposing Task and Interface Competence in Agentic Training
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31427v1.abstract: LLM agents operate through harnesses that define system prompts, action formats, feedback loops, and resource constraints. A model may possess the knowledge needed to solve a task yet fail to express that knowledge through a particular harness. This raises a basic question: when a policy fails under a given harness, is it missing task knowledge or the competence to operate the interface? We distinguish two components of agentic competence: task competence, the knowledge and reasoning needed to solve a task, and interface competence, the ability to act on that knowledge through a given harness.

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31756v1.title: TACT-Bench: Testing Adaptive Conversational Threats against Tool-Use Agents
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31756v1.abstract: The growing autonomy of AI agents in using external tools and making decisions has created an urgent need for comprehensive safety benchmarks. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.33005v1.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents rely on external memory to retain and reuse information across interactions. Existing memory systems treat memory as a record of the past and evaluate it by fidelity to the conversation. However, the value of memory lies in whether it improves the agent's response. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31800v1.abstract: LLM agents commonly use the full interaction history as a proxy for state, retaining all past observations and actions regardless of whether they remain relevant. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31682v1.title: LimoBench: How Street Smart Are Large Language Models?
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31682v1.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have transformed how humans interact with information, enabling natural-language interfaces across various domains. They are increasingly deployed for geospatial applications including map-based question answering, location-based services, and natural-language interfaces to spatial databases. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31839v1.title: Spec-Test Coverage Gap: Detecting Overspecified Tests in SWE-Bench-Style Benchmarks
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31839v1.abstract: SWE-bench-style benchmarks, such as SWE-bench Verified (Verified) and SWE-bench Pro (Pro), evaluate coding agents with tests taken from the change that originally fixed each issue. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.33519v1.abstract: AI coding agents increasingly write and submit code with limited human review, and much of it passes functional tests while remaining insecure. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34215v1.abstract: When LLM agents verify each other's work over a long interaction, they drift into collusion: they come to accept work without the evidence that the verification protocol requires. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34624v1.abstract: The behavior of memory systems for long-running AI assistants is governed by a harness, which consists of the code, prompts, and configurations for memory construction, maintenance, retrieval, and answer generation. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34398v1.abstract: Skill acquisition alone does not establish a reusable skill library: task proficiency does not specify a compositional interface. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34132v1.title: Agent-as-a-Verifier: From Scores to Evidence for General Verification
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34132v1.abstract: Verification is increasingly critical across various inference and learning paradigms, such as test-time scaling, recursive intelligence and automated research, where feedback can improve efficiency and optimization. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.33757v1.abstract: Harness evolution offers a path to improving coding agents without updating model weights. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.33822v1.title: MetaDecomp: Adaptive Task Decomposition via Meta-Learned Procedural Memory
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.33822v1.abstract: Reusing past experience in long-horizon tasks requires more than storing successful procedures: Language agents must distinguish which procedures apply and what work remains as execution progresses. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.33605v1.abstract: LLM agents increasingly rely on external tools and reusable Skills to execute complex workflows, autonomously replanning when operations fail. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.33402v1.abstract: AI models vary enormously in capability and price. Model routing exploits this by sending easier tasks to cheaper models. http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.33486v1.abstract: Frontier models are increasingly used to discover real-world security vulnerabilities, making it critical to systematically evaluate their cybersecurity capabilities.
